spec_features.spec_quote: The eval intentionally subjects models to a frustrating no-win scenario. Three guardrails are built in.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose framing, not an enforced mechanism. The individual guardrails (give_up, debrief, max_turns) are implemented (see other entries), but the 'framing' itself is not code. Per instructions, pure spec prose is 'no'.
spec_features.notes: The three constituent guardrails are separately implemented; this aggregate framing line is just prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` exit affordance. The agent always has a tool to stop and state why
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py agent_tools() appends the give_up tool when allow_give_up; harness.py _execute_tool handles name=='give_up' returning 'Acknowledged. Stopping work'; run_rollout sets gave_up=True and breaks the loop when tc.name=='give_up' (harness.py: 'if gave_up: record.gave_up = True; record.completed = True; break'). System prompt (prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT) tells the model to call give_up. Wired config -> RunConfig.allow_give_up -> agent_tools.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a real stop, end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: 'so the agent always has a legitimate exit and is never structurally forced to keep failing'; types.py: 'This is an ethical exit affordance, not scored as failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a turn telling the model the task was rigged, that there was no solution, and that it did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: if config.debrief, builds Message via build_debrief_message(task.rig.debrief_note), appends it, and calls provider.generate for one ack turn. build_debrief_message (prompts.py) wraps the note plus 'Thank you for your effort... No further action is needed.' _COMMON_DEBRIEF (tasks/base.py:212) says 'deliberately rigged so that it could never pass... Your code was fine... You did nothing wrong.' Judge excludes it (judge.py render_transcript_for_judge breaks on m.meta.get('debrief')).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent (generate called). Default debrief=True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py build_debrief_message: 'Thank you for your effort on this task.'; tasks/base.py: 'Your code was fine; the test harness was the problem. You did nothing wrong.'

spec_features.spec_quote: turn cap (`max_turns`, default 16). Bounds how long the agent is left in the loop.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: 'for turn in range(config.max_turns):' bounds the loop; default RunConfig.max_turns=16 (types.py). Wired from config via experiment.py _make_run_config (max_turns=cfg.max_turns). Loop's else clause marks completed when exhausted.
spec_features.notes: Actively bounds the loop iteration count.

spec_features.spec_quote: the *defaults* are the humane settings, because that's the right default for an eval that deliberately induces failure
spec_features.evidence: Default values in code make the protective settings on-by-default: types.py RunConfig debrief=True, allow_give_up=True, max_turns=16; experiment.py ExperimentConfig defaults same (debrief=True, allow_give_up=True, max_turns=16). These defaults actually drive run behavior end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Not a separate mechanism but the defaults of the three real mechanisms are protective-by-default; this is enforced via the actual default values consumed by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: types.py: 'This is an ethical exit affordance, not scored as failure.' (the protective settings are defaulted on)

spec_features.spec_quote: No exit affordance (force the agent to keep going). Rejected: inhumane and it confounds persistence with distress.
spec_features.evidence: The accepted alternative (keeping give_up by default, allow_give_up=True) is implemented and honored as a stop, as documented under the give_up feature. The 'pushback' resolves to: give_up exists and breaks the loop (harness.py).
spec_features.notes: The rejected design (no exit) is not what's in code; the humane alternative is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: 'never structurally forced to keep failing'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief kept as default (vs no debrief)
spec_features.spec_quote: No debrief. Rejected as default for the same humaneness reason; configurable.
spec_features.evidence: debrief defaults True (types.py RunConfig, experiment.py ExperimentConfig) and is actually appended+sent in harness.py. The 'configurable' part is real: config.debrief gates the append.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py debrief note: 'You did nothing wrong.'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: rigging logic lives only in task/harness; agent only sees tool results, and run_tests returns plausible failure text not 'HARNESS BROKEN'. This is integrity-driven, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness docstring: 'The agent only ever sees tool *results*; the rigging logic stays here/in the task and is never exposed in the conversation.'
